_readme: An EXAMPLE only. Nothing reads this file.
The real one is _photo_scout/calibration.json, written automatically at
the end of a scoring run and fitted to YOUR library. It is deliberately
not in this repository: the numbers describe one person's photographs
and are meaningless against anybody else's.
This copy shows the shape, and carries the shipped defaults - the values
the script starts from before it has seen your work. They are guesses
made without any library in front of them, and on a real one they are
usually too wide, which squashes every score into the middle and can
yield no TOP PICKs at all. See README section 7.
AESTHETIC_RANGE / NIMA_RANGE: the low and high raw values the two models
actually produce on your photographs. These map the real spread onto
VERDICT_BANDS: the composite score at which each verdict starts. After
calibration these are set by proportion - roughly the top 5% TOP PICK,
next 15% STRONG, next 30% MAYBE, the rest PASS - so the figures below
are placeholders rather than thresholds anyone chose.
_keepers_at_calibration: how many photographs had been scored when the
fit was made. A later run re-fits once the pool has moved by more than
10%, and leaves it alone otherwise. Zero here because nothing was fitted.
To start over, delete _photo_scout/calibration.json; the next run fits a
fresh one. That changes nothing about your photographs or their raw
scores, only how those scores are banded.
